teams.heading: Fiji Latui reduced to 12 men in nine-try rout by Ireland XV
teams.body: Fiji's second-string Latui side conceded nine tries to an Ireland XV at Virgin Media Park on Friday, collecting four first-half yellow cards and, at one stage, playing with 12 men. Tighthead Mesake Doge was binned for a high tackle, then shown a second yellow — a 20-minute red card — 30 seconds after returning, for collapsing a scrum. Isaia Lotawa's no-arms tackle conceded a penalty try, and Apisalome Kuruisaqila was carded for a deliberate knock-on. Pita Lesivoukionoilau's intercept try, converted by Joeli Baleilevuka, gave the Latui their only lead.

lead.why: It is the only new event about a Fijian side, and a card-strewn collapse of Fiji's development team is the story fans will be talking about.

teams.heading: Former captain Lewis Moody joins England to face the All Blacks' haka
teams.body: Moody, diagnosed with motor neurone disease last year, stood between captain Maro Itoje and vice-captain Ellis Genge before Saturday's 37-12 win at Allianz Stadium, then delivered the match ball. Fellow vice-captains Ollie Chessum and Jamie George led the side forward into a V, and every England player wore boots bearing the logo of Moody's Front Up to MND campaign. Head coach Steve Borthwick said Moody had handed out the shirts the night before, telling BBC Radio 5 Live: "It was some way to start a big game of rugby."

teams.heading: Jean-Baptiste Gros ruled out of Argentina test, Rodrigue Neti promoted to start
teams.body: France loosehead Jean-Baptiste Gros was ruled out on Saturday of the Nations Championship meeting with Argentina after being judged too short of fitness. The Toulon forward had been excused training at Marcoussis on Wednesday, yet head coach Fabien Galthié still named him in the starting XV on Thursday. Toulouse's Rodrigue Neti, a replacement against South Africa, was named to start instead. Jefferson Poirot, who missed that Springbok win with concussion, stayed on the bench. Rugbyrama reported that Gros could miss the rest of the competition.

lead.why: A late injury withdrawal from the named XV is fresh hard news about France's own side.

teams.heading: Robert Baloucoune scores twice as Ireland edge Springboks 20-17 in Dublin
teams.body: Ulster wing Robert Baloucoune had Ireland ahead inside eight minutes of Saturday's Nations Championship test at the Aviva Stadium, then crossed again before the break. Two missed Sam Prendergast conversions let South Africa draw level, but Rónan Kelleher's try in the corner made it 17-10 at half-time. A Prendergast penalty stretched the lead before Malcolm Marx's Springbok try, with just over 20 minutes left, set up a nervy finish. Balls.ie notes it is Ireland's first win over South Africa, France or New Zealand since July 2024.

lead.why: The senior side's 20-17 win over South Africa has not yet run, and this is the only item with match detail.

teams.heading: Prop Simone Ferrari ruled out of Fiji defeat an hour before kick-off
teams.body: OnRugby reports that tighthead Simone Ferrari injured his left arm during the build-up in Udine, and his recovery time will be assessed in the coming days. Marco Riccioni, originally named on the bench, was promoted to the No. 3 shirt, and fellow tighthead Ion Neculai came into the 23 at 18. The reshuffled side, captained by hooker Giacomo Nicotera, went down 16-21 to Fiji. It was a sixth loss in six, and it leaves Italy 12th of 12 on the log.

lead.why: A late injury and forced change to Italy's front row is fresh hard news about the senior side.

teams.heading: Gregor Townsend says points blitz leaves Scotland's Twickenham finals week undecided
teams.body: Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend admitted his side had one eye on the scoreboard during the 67-5 rout of Japan, telling BBC Scotland that reaching a points total was an ambition the players delivered. The consequence is uncertainty over the finals weekend at Twickenham: "We don't know what our week's going to look like," he said, adding that without the points haul the schedule would already have been settled. SA Rugby Magazine reports Scotland stay fourth in the northern hemisphere table, but with a vastly improved points difference.

lead.why: Townsend's admission that Scotland chased a points total, leaving their Twickenham finals week unsettled, is the fresh forward-looking angle beyond the already-run hat-tricks.

teams.heading: WRU counts 68 Wales players to beat All Blacks after Cardiff win
teams.body: The 23 men who beat New Zealand 35-28 at Principality Stadium on 14 November have taken the roll of Wales players to have beaten the All Blacks from 45 to 68, the Welsh Rugby Union has noted. They join the sides of 1905, 1935 and 1953. The WRU also points out that fans celebrated in the same Cardiff pubs as after those earlier wins, the City Arms, the Angel Hotel and Queen's Vaults among them. A celebratory pint, it adds, has risen from 1½p in 1905 to around £5.25.

lead.why: The team-change and 'not fixed' stories have already run, and Liam Wright is Australia's story, so the WRU's All Blacks roll of honour is the freshest Wales item.

teams.heading: French federation honours Federico Martín Aramburu with son in Pumas shirt
teams.body: The French Rugby Federation arranged for the late Argentine's son to walk out in an Argentina jersey before Saturday's test against France. He would hold the hands of both captains, Argentina's Julián Montoya and France scrum-half Antoine Dupont, in recognition of his dual nationality. A minute's applause was planned at the Stade de France. Martín Aramburu, a former Argentine player well known in the French championship in the early 2000s, was killed in a Paris street in 2022, aged 42. Two far-right activists were sentenced to 26 and 19 years.

lead.why: The only new item centred on Argentina, involving the Pumas captain and a former Argentine player.

teams.heading: Wallabies faced Wales needing Argentina to slip for an Ireland final
teams.body: Australia went into Saturday's final round-robin test in Cardiff fourth in the Nations Championship's Southern Hemisphere pool, two points behind Argentina, who played France simultaneously, Rugby.com.au reported. Victory over Wales plus an Argentina defeat would send head coach Les Kiss's side to Allianz Stadium, Twickenham, to face Ireland in the third-ranked final. Most other combinations, especially an Argentina win, meant a Finals Weekend rematch with Scotland, who beat Australia 15-12 in Round 5. Wales arrived on the back of a 35-28 win over the All Blacks.

lead.why: The Liam Wright eligibility story has already run, so the Finals Weekend stakes riding on the Cardiff test are the freshest different Australia story.

teams.heading: Murrayfield rout leaves Japan's fifth place at the mercy of Fiji
teams.body: Italian outlet OnRugby reckons Saturday's 67-5 defeat to Scotland could cost head coach Eddie Jones' side fifth place among the southern hemisphere teams in the Nations Championship, should Fiji beat Italy with a bonus point and a healthy margin. The round-six loss followed last week's 78-15 hammering by England. Ahead of the trip to Edinburgh, RugbyAsia247 had Japan heading for a bottom or second-bottom pool finish, potentially setting up a finals-weekend meeting with Wales or Italy.

teams.heading: Guardian's Gerard Meagher brands Beauden Barrett a symbol of All Blacks' decline
teams.body: Saturday's 37-12 defeat by England should have been Beauden Barrett's day. The All Blacks full-back became just the fourth man to play 150 Tests and scored a try, converted by Damian McKenzie, that cut the gap to 24-12. The Guardian's Gerard Meagher instead cast the fading veteran as emblematic of the side's joyless decline. He called the handling "shocking, hesitant in possession" after head coach Dave Rennie's public rebuke following the Wales loss. He conceded mitigation: half a team, including Ardie Savea, is on the injury list.

lead.why: The result has already run, so Barrett's soured 150th Test and the Guardian's verdict on it is the freshest New Zealand angle.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus risks breaching suspension with online watchalong of Dublin defeat
teams.body: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus streamed himself watching Saturday's 20-17 loss to Ireland from his Dublin hotel. Sky Sports reports the free broadcast could breach his six-match World Rugby ban, which forbids "direct or indirect contact with team management or players on matchdays." Muted for both halves, he was seen clapping, apparently shouting into a phone and thumping the table as Ireland closed out the win. At half-time he unmuted to say: "If we step it up I think we'll be in this match."

lead.why: A fresh matchday event involving the suspended Springbok coach, not a pundit's take on the ban.
